To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the parameter selection techniques based on Pearson correlations, Sobol indices and Morris indices, all perform well, and that the verification techniques based on standard errors and Sobol indices, both based on second-order models, perform well.

(i) the Pearson correlation coefficient and standard errors are not suitable for parameter selection, and (ii) Sobol and Morris indices are useful for parameter selection but can be misleading for verification.

(1) global sensitivity analysis techniques based on the Pearson coefficient, Sobol, and Morris indices are useful tools for parameter selection and verification in the context of HIV models and (2) verification strategies are necessary to assess the reliability of those techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the selection and verification of influential parameters for dynamic biological and physical models.

the development and verification of parameter selection and verification tools that are useful for a wide range of nonlinear dynamic models, with a focus on those that are used to describe biological systems.

the selection and verification of parameters in a model that minimizes the number of influential parameters, which is important in the design of experiments, as well as for the validation and verification of model predictions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the techniques are useful and reliable, provided that the user is careful in their application.
the parameter selection technique based upon the Pearson correlation coefficient is a reliable and robust technique for identifying influential and noninfluential parameters.
parameter selection and verification strategies based on global sensitivity analysis are effective and can be used to select and verify parameters that are non-influential for the HIV model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, when a model is used to predict a quantity that is a function of multiple outputs (such as the total amount of virus over time), the parameter selection and parameter verification techniques that we present are effective and accurate.
the parameter selection techniques based on global sensitivity analysis are accurate, provided the verification strategy is applied.

, for the HIV model, the parameter selection techniques based on the Pearson coefficient and the second-order model representation are more accurate than those based on the standard error, whereas all techniques perform reasonably well for the verification task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parameter selection techniques can be applied to the HIV model with confidence, but the parameter verification techniques should be applied with some caution.
parameter selection and verification are not only important for the development of mathematical models, but also for their application in the context of model-based inference.
the parameter selection techniques can be used to identify noninfluential parameters and the verification techniques can be used for a quantitative assessment of the accuracy of these techniques.
